subproblems.title: Smooth cutoff: χ = 1 near a compact K, 0 ≤ χ ≤ 1, compact support inside an open U
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open and K ⊆ U compact (ℝ^P = Eucl P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P)). Then there are a C^∞ function χ : ℝ^P → ℝ (ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) χ) and an open set N ⊆ ℝ^P such that 0 ≤ χ(x) ≤ 1 for every x, χ has compact support (HasCompactSupport χ), tsupport χ ⊆ U, K ⊆ N and χ(x) = 1 for every x ∈ N.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (U K : Set (Eucl P)), IsOpen U → IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → ∃ (χ : Eucl P → ℝ) (N : Set (Eucl P)), ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) χ ∧ (∀ x, 0 ≤ χ x ∧ χ x ≤ 1) ∧ HasCompactSupport χ ∧ tsupport χ ⊆ U ∧ IsOpen N ∧ K ⊆ N ∧ ∀ x ∈ N, χ x = 1
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 1 (Cutoff) of the parent proof of fiw_tb_extend_to_univ, written out for ℝ^P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P). This is a finite-dimensional real normed space, hence locally compact and Hausdorff, so its compact subsets are closed.

1. (Two compact neighbourhoods.) K is compact, U is open and K ⊆ U. By local compactness there is a compact set L with K ⊆ interior L and L ⊆ U (Mathlib exists_compact_between). Apply the same fact to K and the open set interior L (isOpen_interior; K ⊆ interior L). This gives a compact set L₁ with K ⊆ interior L₁ and L₁ ⊆ interior L.
2. (Smooth Urysohn function.) L₁ is compact, hence closed; interior L is open; and L₁ ⊆ interior L. The smooth Urysohn lemma for finite-dimensional real normed spaces (Mathlib exists_contDiff_support_eq_eq_one_iff with smoothness n := (⊤ : ℕ∞), s := interior L, t := L₁) gives f : ℝ^P → ℝ with:
   - ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) f;
   - range f ⊆ [0, 1];
   - support f = interior L;
   - for every x, x ∈ L₁ ⟺ f(x) = 1.
   (Alternatively, use exists_contMDiffMap_one_nhds_of_subset_interior with the model 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ^P), s := K, t := L, then contMDiff_iff_contDiff. The argument below only needs the listed properties.)
3. Put χ := f and N := interior L₁.
   (a) χ is C^∞ by step 2.
   (b) For every x, χ(x) ∈ range f ⊆ [0, 1], i.e. 0 ≤ χ(x) ≤ 1.
   (c) support χ = interior L ⊆ L, and L is closed. So tsupport χ = closure(support χ) ⊆ L (closure_minimal), hence tsupport χ ⊆ L ⊆ U.
   (d) tsupport χ is closed (isClosed_tsupport) and contained in the compact set L, so it is compact (IsCompact.of_isClosed_subset). That is, HasCompactSupport χ.
   (e) N = interior L₁ is open (isOpen_interior), and K ⊆ N by step 1.
   (f) If x ∈ N then x ∈ L₁ (interior_subset), so χ(x) = 1 by step 2.
4. Properties (a)–(f) are exactly the assertions of the lemma. ∎

  intro P U K hU hK hKU
  obtain ⟨L, hL, hKL, hLU⟩ := exists_compact_between hK hU hKU
  obtain ⟨L₁, hL₁, hKL₁, hL₁L⟩ := exists_compact_between hK isOpen_interior hKL
  obtain ⟨f, hf, hfr, hfs, hf1⟩ :=
    exists_contDiff_support_eq_eq_one_iff (n := (⊤ : ℕ∞)) isOpen_interior hL₁.isClosed hL₁L
  have htsupp : tsupport f ⊆ L :=
    closure_minimal (hfs.symm ▸ interior_subset) hL.isClosed
  refine ⟨f, interior L₁, hf, fun x => hfr (mem_range_self x), ?_, htsupp.trans hLU,
    isOpen_interior, hKL₁, fun x hx => (hf1 x).mp (interior_subset hx)⟩
  exact hL.of_isClosed_subset (isClosed_tsupport _) htsupp

Smooth Urysohn (exists_contDiff_support_eq_eq_one_iff): f is C^∞ with values in [0, 1], support f = interior L, and f = 1 exactly on L₁.
tsupport f ⊆ L because L is closed; hence f has compact support contained in U.
N := interior L₁ is open, contains K, and f = 1 on N.

subproblems.title: Multiplying test forms by a smooth function supported in W is a linear map D^q(V) → D^q(W)
subproblems.statement: Let P, q ∈ ℕ, let V, W ⊆ ℝ^P be arbitrary sets, and let χ : ℝ^P → ℝ be C^∞ (ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) χ) with tsupport χ ⊆ W. Then there is an ℝ-linear map L : D^q(V) → D^q(W) (TestFormOn V q →ₗ[ℝ] TestFormOn W q) such that (Lω)(x) = χ(x)·ω(x) for every ω ∈ D^q(V) and every x ∈ ℝ^P. This is an identity of underlying forms; χ(x)·ω(x) is the scalar multiple of the covector ω(x).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P q : ℕ) (V W : Set (Eucl P)) (χ : Eucl P → ℝ), ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) χ → tsupport χ ⊆ W → ∃ L : TestFormOn V q →ₗ[ℝ] TestFormOn W q, ∀ (ω : TestFormOn V q) (x : Eucl P), (L ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) q) x = χ x • (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) q) x
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 2 (Products with χ) of the parent proof, for arbitrary source and target domains.

Notation. For ω ∈ D^q(V) = TestFormOn V q we also write ω for the underlying form (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) q). By definition of TestFormOn (testFormOnSubmodule), a form φ : ℝ^P → Covector (Eucl P) q belongs to TestFormOn W q iff:
- φ is C^∞ (IsSmoothForm φ, i.e. ContDiff ℝ ∞ φ);
- HasCompactSupport φ;
- tsupport φ ⊆ W.
The vector-space operations of TestFormOn W q are pointwise. Two elements are equal iff their underlying forms are equal (Subtype.ext).

1. Fix ω ∈ D^q(V) and put φ_ω(x) := χ(x)·ω(x).
   (a) Smoothness. χ : ℝ^P → ℝ is C^∞, and ω : ℝ^P → Covector (Eucl P) q is C^∞ since ω ∈ D^q(V). So the pointwise scalar product φ_ω is C^∞ (ContDiff.smul).
   (b) Compact support.
       - tsupport φ_ω ⊆ tsupport ω (tsupport_smul_subset_right), and tsupport ω is compact (HasCompactSupport ω).
       - tsupport φ_ω is closed (isClosed_tsupport), so it is compact (IsCompact.of_isClosed_subset), i.e. HasCompactSupport φ_ω.
       - No compactness of tsupport χ is needed.
   (c) Support in W. tsupport φ_ω ⊆ tsupport χ ⊆ W, by tsupport_smul_subset_left and the hypothesis.
   Hence φ_ω ∈ TestFormOn W q.
2. Define L(ω) := ⟨φ_ω, step 1⟩ ∈ D^q(W). By construction (Lω)(x) = χ(x)·ω(x) for all x.
3. L is ℝ-linear. Both identities are checked on underlying forms at every point x (Subtype.ext, funext):
   (a) L(ω₁ + ω₂)(x) = χ(x)·(ω₁(x) + ω₂(x)) = χ(x)·ω₁(x) + χ(x)·ω₂(x) = (Lω₁ + Lω₂)(x) (smul_add);
   (b) for c ∈ ℝ, L(cω)(x) = χ(x)·(c·ω(x)) = c·(χ(x)·ω(x)) = (c·Lω)(x) (smul_comm).
   So L, with map_add' from (a) and map_smul' from (b), is a linear map TestFormOn V q →ₗ[ℝ] TestFormOn W q.
4. L satisfies the asserted pointwise formula (step 2). ∎

  intro P q V W χ hχ hχW
  have hmem : ∀ ω : TestFormOn V q,
      (fun x => χ x • (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) q) x) ∈ TestFormOn W q := by
    intro ω
    obtain ⟨⟨hs, hc⟩, -⟩ := ω.property
    refine ⟨⟨hχ.smul hs, ?_⟩, (tsupport_smul_subset_left _ _).trans hχW⟩
    exact hc.of_isClosed_subset (isClosed_tsupport _) (tsupport_smul_subset_right _ _)
  refine ⟨{ toFun := fun ω => ⟨_, hmem ω⟩, map_add' := ?_, map_smul' := ?_ }, fun ω x => rfl⟩
  · intro a b
    apply Subtype.ext
    funext x
    change χ x • ((a : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) q) x + (b : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) q) x) = _
    rw [smul_add]
    rfl
  · intro c a
    apply Subtype.ext
    funext x
    change χ x • (c • (a : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) q) x) =
      c • (χ x • (a : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) q) x)
    rw [smul_comm]
proof_key_steps: For ω ∈ D^q(V), χ·ω is C^∞ (ContDiff.smul), has compact support (tsupport ⊆ tsupport ω), and tsupport ⊆ tsupport χ ⊆ W, so χ·ω ∈ D^q(W).
L(ω) := χ·ω satisfies the pointwise formula by construction.
Additivity and homogeneity hold pointwise (smul_add, smul_comm), so L is linear.

subproblems.title: A current vanishing off K only sees test forms on a neighbourhood of K
subproblems.statement: Let P, q ∈ ℕ and V, K, N ⊆ ℝ^P with N open and K ⊆ N. Let Z ∈ D_q(V) (GeometricCurrentOn V q) satisfy Z(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ D^q(V) (TestFormOn V q) whose tsupport is disjoint from K. Then Z(η) = Z(ω) for all ω, η ∈ D^q(V) with η(x) = ω(x) for every x ∈ N.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P q : ℕ) (V K N : Set (Eucl P)) (Z : GeometricCurrentOn V q), IsOpen N → K ⊆ N → (∀ ω : TestFormOn V q, Disjoint (tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) q)) K → Z ω = 0) → ∀ ω η : TestFormOn V q, (∀ x ∈ N, (η : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) q) x = (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) q) x) → Z η = Z ω
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 3 (vanishing fact (V)) of the parent proof, in the form used in steps 5, 8 and (B5). There η = χ•ω with χ = 1 on N, so η and ω agree on N. The hypothesis "Z vanishes on test forms supported off K" replaces the parent's appeal to spt Z ⊆ K and vanish_off_support; the parent derives this hypothesis from spt Z ⊆ K.

1. Put ζ := η − ω ∈ D^q(V). D^q(V) is a real vector space with pointwise operations, so ζ(x) = η(x) − ω(x). For x ∈ N, ζ(x) = 0 by hypothesis. Hence support ζ ⊆ ℝ^P ∖ N.
2. N is open, so ℝ^P ∖ N is closed. Therefore tsupport ζ = closure(support ζ) ⊆ ℝ^P ∖ N (closure_minimal).
3. K ⊆ N, so ℝ^P ∖ N is disjoint from K. By step 2, tsupport ζ is disjoint from K.
4. By the hypothesis on Z, Z(ζ) = 0. Z is linear (Z.toCurrent is a linear map; map_sub), so Z(ζ) = Z(η) − Z(ω). Hence Z(η) = Z(ω). ∎

  intro P q V K N Z hN hKN hZ ω η hηω
  have hsupp : tsupport ((η - ω : TestFormOn V q) : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) q) ⊆ Nᶜ := by
    apply closure_minimal _ hN.isClosed_compl
    intro x hx hxN
    apply hx
    change (η : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) q) x - (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) q) x = 0
    rw [hηω x hxN, sub_self]
  have h0 : Z (η - ω) = 0 :=
    hZ _ (Disjoint.mono_left hsupp (disjoint_compl_left.mono_right hKN))

subproblems.title: Homogeneity of the Euclidean coefficient norm: |cα| = |c|·|α|
subproblems.statement: For all P, q ∈ ℕ, every c ∈ ℝ and every q-covector α ∈ Covector (Eucl P) q: covectorEuclideanNorm (c • α) = |c| · covectorEuclideanNorm α. Here covectorEuclideanNorm α = √(Σ_{I : Fin q → Fin P} t_I(α)), where t_I(α) = α(e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(q−1)})² if I is strictly increasing and t_I(α) = 0 otherwise, and e_i = EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ i.

Source: the homogeneity fact |tα| = |t|·|α| stated in the Notation paragraph and used in step 4(a) of the parent proof. It is also step 1 of the accepted proof of br_la_abs_apply_le_mul_mass.

1. Scalar multiplication of continuous alternating maps is pointwise (ContinuousAlternatingMap.smul_apply). So for every I : Fin q → Fin P, (c • α)(e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(q−1)}) = c·α(e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(q−1)}).
   - For strictly increasing I: t_I(c • α) = (c·α(e_I))² = c²·t_I(α) (mul_pow).
   - For the other I: t_I(c • α) = 0 = c²·t_I(α).
2. Summing over the finitely many I gives Σ_I t_I(c • α) = c²·s, where s := Σ_I t_I(α) ≥ 0 (Finset.mul_sum).
3. Therefore:
   covectorEuclideanNorm (c • α) = √(c²·s)
   = √(c²)·√s (Real.sqrt_mul, as c² ≥ 0)
   = |c|·√s (Real.sqrt_sq_eq_abs)
   = |c|·covectorEuclideanNorm α. ∎

An n-covector α is a continuous alternating n-linear map (ℝ^P)ⁿ → ℝ with the operator norm ‖α‖ (least C with |α(u₁,…,u_n)| ≤ C Π|u_i|); an n-vector is a continuous linear functional on n-covectors with the operator norm; simpleNVector v is the n-vector α ↦ α(v₁,…,v_n), so |simpleNVector v (α)| ≤ ‖α‖ Π|v_i|; for a linear map A, A_# w := nVectorPushforward n A w = w ∘ A^#, where A^#α = α(A·,…,A·), it is linear in w and A_#(simpleNVector v) = simpleNVector(A v) (`nVectorPushforward_simple`). A map Φ is c-antilipschitz on Ω if c|w − w′| ≤ |Φ(w) − Φ(w′)| for all w, w′ ∈ Ω.

This is item (P2) of the parent proof. Recall spt T = T.support = U ∖ Z_T, where Z_T (the zero region) is the union of all open W with closure W compact, closure W ⊆ U, on which T vanishes (T(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ Dⁿ(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W).

1. Since M ⊆ U (field `subset`), M ∖ spt T ⊆ Z_T.

2. Z_T is an open subset of the second countable space ℝ^P, hence Lindelöf; so there are countably many sets W_k of the defining family with Z_T = ⋃_k W_k. By countable subadditivity it suffices to prove Hⁿ(M ∩ W) = 0 for every open W with K := closure W compact, K ⊆ U, on which T vanishes.

3. (ξ has unit norm a.e.) By the field `orients`, for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M there is an orthonormal τ : Fin n → ℝ^P with ξ(x) = simpleNVector τ or ξ(x) = −simpleNVector τ. By the sibling lemma simple_nvector_algebra (first conjunct, with G(τ) = I), ‖simpleNVector τ‖² = det I = 1. Hence ‖ξ(x)‖ = 1 for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M; in particular ξ(x) ≠ 0 and |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ ‖α‖ for every n-covector α. (If no orthonormal n-family exists, e.g. n > P, this a.e. statement already forces Hⁿ(M) = 0 and the lemma holds; the argument below covers this case too.)

4. Fix W and K as in step 2. θ > 0 on M (field `pos`) and θ is Hⁿ-integrable on M ∩ K (field `integrableOn`, K compact ⊆ U). Let ν be the finite Borel measure ν(B) := ∫_{B ∩ M ∩ W} θ dHⁿ (ν = θ·Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ W)); ν(ℝ^P) ≤ ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞.

5. Fix an n-covector α and φ ∈ C_c^∞(ℝ^P) with tsupport φ ⊆ W. The form ω(x) := φ(x)α is smooth with compact support contained in W ⊆ U, so ω ∈ Dⁿ(U) and T(ω) = 0 because T vanishes on W. By the representation T = τ(M,θ,ξ):
 0 = T(ω) = ∫_M θ(x) ξ(x)(φ(x)α) dHⁿ(x) = ∫_M φ(x) θ(x) ξ(x)(α) dHⁿ(x) = ∫ φ g_α dν, with g_α(x) := ξ(x)(α),
 where we used that φ = 0 off W; all integrands are absolutely integrable since |φ θ ξ(α)| ≤ sup|φ| ‖α‖ θ 1_{M∩K} Hⁿ-a.e. on M by step 3.

6. g_α is ν-measurable (ξ is Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. strongly measurable, field `aestronglyMeasurable`, and ν ≪ Hⁿ⌞M) and |g_α| ≤ ‖α‖ ν-a.e., so g_α is ν-integrable, hence locally ν-integrable on W. As ν is a finite (so locally finite) Borel measure and ∫ φ g_α dν = 0 for all φ ∈ C_c^∞ with tsupport in the open set W, the fundamental lemma of the calculus of variations (Mathlib `IsOpen.ae_eq_zero_of_integral_contDiff_smul_eq_zero`; equivalently: the finite signed measure g_α ν⌞W annihilates C_c^∞(W), hence by uniform approximation of C_c(W) by mollification annihilates C_c(W), hence is the zero measure) gives g_α = 0 ν-a.e. on W.

7. Because θ > 0 on M, a subset of M ∩ W is ν-null iff it is Hⁿ-null. Hence ξ(x)(α) = 0 for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M ∩ W. Let α₁,…,α_N be a basis of the finite-dimensional space of n-covectors on ℝ^P; intersecting the N full-measure sets, for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M ∩ W the linear functional ξ(x) vanishes on a basis, so ξ(x) = 0.

9. By steps 1, 2 and 8, Hⁿ(M ∖ spt T) ≤ Σ_k Hⁿ(M ∩ W_k) = 0. ∎ (For n = 0 the same proof applies: 0-covectors are constants and ‖simpleNVector ∅‖ = 1.)

Since ξ ≠ 0 a.e. on M, Hⁿ(M ∩ W) = 0; sum over the countable cover.

Notation. H := Hᵏ = `μHE[k]` on ℝ^P. For r > 0, η_r(y) := r⁻¹(y − x) (`blowUpMap x r`). By definition, `HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt k M θ x L` means: dim L = k (`finrank ℝ L = k`), and for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P;ℝ), I_{M,θ}(r) := ∫_{η_r(M)} f(y)θ(x + ry) dH(y) → θ(x)∫_L f dH as r ↓ 0 (limit along 𝓝[>]0).

1. (Null sets under blow-up.) If r > 0 and H(Z) = 0 then H(η_r(Z)) = 0. Indeed |η_r(a) − η_r(b)| = r⁻¹|a − b|, so η_r is Lipschitz with constant r⁻¹ and μH[k](η_r(Z)) ≤ r^{−k}μH[k](Z) (Mathlib `LipschitzWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le`). Moreover H = c_k·μH[k] with c_k ∈ (0,∞) (`euclideanHausdorffMeasure_def`, `addHaarScalarFactor_volume_hausdorffMeasure_ne_zero`), so H(Z) = 0 ⇒ μH[k](Z) = 0 ⇒ μH[k](η_r(Z)) = 0 ⇒ H(η_r(Z)) = 0.
2. (Elementary facts on η_r.) For r > 0, η_r is a bijection of ℝ^P with inverse y ↦ x + ry. Hence η_r(A ∩ B) = η_r(A) ∩ η_r(B), η_r(A ∖ B) = η_r(A) ∖ η_r(B) for all A, B, and η_r(V) = {y : x + ry ∈ V} is open (preimage of the open V under a continuous map).
3. (Reduction.) The dimension conditions for (M,θ) and (M′,θ′) are the same condition on L. Fix f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P;ℝ). Choose R > 0 with f(y) = 0 whenever |y| ≥ R (tsupport f is compact, hence bounded), and δ > 0 with B_δ(x) ⊆ V (V open, x ∈ V). We prove I_{M,θ}(r) = I_{M′,θ′}(r) for every r ∈ (0, δ/R). Since (0, δ/R) ∈ 𝓝[>]0, the two functions of r agree eventually as r ↓ 0, so I_{M′,θ′}(r) has the same limit θ(x)∫_L f dH, which equals θ′(x)∫_L f dH because θ(x) = θ′(x). This gives `HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt k M′ θ′ x L`.
4. (Integrands vanish off η_r(V).) Let r ∈ (0, δ/R), g : ℝ^P → ℝ arbitrary, F_g(y) := f(y)g(x + ry). If y ∉ η_r(V) then x + ry ∉ V ⊇ B_δ(x), so r|y| ≥ δ, hence |y| ≥ δ/r > R, f(y) = 0 and F_g(y) = 0.
5. (Step A: cutting by V.) For every S ⊆ ℝ^P and every g: ∫_{η_r(S)} F_g dH = ∫_{η_r(S∩V)} F_g dH. Indeed η_r(S ∩ V) = η_r(S) ∩ η_r(V) (step 2); since η_r(V) is open (measurable), H⌞(η_r(V) ∩ η_r(S)) = (H⌞η_r(S))⌞η_r(V) (`Measure.restrict_restrict`); and the integral of F_g with respect to (H⌞η_r(S))⌞η_r(V) equals its integral with respect to H⌞η_r(S), because F_g vanishes off η_r(V) (step 4; `setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero`).
6. (Step C: replacing θ by θ′.) ∫_{η_r(M∩V)} F_θ dH = ∫_{η_r(M∩V)} F_{θ′} dH. By hypothesis (H⌞(M∩V)){z : θ(z) ≠ θ′(z)} = 0, so there is a Borel set N ⊇ {z : θ(z) ≠ θ′(z)} with (H⌞(M∩V))(N) = H(N ∩ (M∩V)) = 0 (`exists_measurable_superset_of_null`, `Measure.restrict_apply`). Let N′ := {y : x + ry ∈ N}, a Borel set. Then {y : F_θ(y) ≠ F_{θ′}(y)} ⊆ N′, and N′ ∩ η_r(M∩V) ⊆ η_r(N ∩ (M∩V)) (if y = η_r(z) with z ∈ M ∩ V and x + ry = z ∈ N). By step 1 the right side is H-null, so (H⌞η_r(M∩V))(N′) = H(N′ ∩ η_r(M∩V)) = 0; thus F_θ = F_{θ′} (H⌞η_r(M∩V))-a.e. and the integrals agree (`integral_congr_ae`).
7. (Step B: replacing M by M′.) η_r(M∩V) and η_r(M′∩V) are H-a.e. equal sets: by step 2 their differences are η_r((M∩V)∖(M′∩V)) and η_r((M′∩V)∖(M∩V)), both contained in η_r((M Δ M′) ∩ V), which is H-null by the hypothesis H((M Δ M′) ∩ V) = 0 and step 1. Hence H⌞η_r(M∩V) = H⌞η_r(M′∩V) (`ae_eq_set`, `Measure.restrict_congr_set`).
8. (Conclusion.) For r ∈ (0, δ/R): I_{M,θ}(r) = ∫_{η_r(M∩V)}F_θ dH (step 5) = ∫_{η_r(M∩V)}F_{θ′} dH (step 6) = ∫_{η_r(M′∩V)}F_{θ′} dH (step 7) = I_{M′,θ′}(r) (step 5 applied to M′, θ′). By step 3 the lemma is proved. No measurability of M, M′, θ, θ′ is used.
proof_key_steps: Blow-up maps η_r(y) = r⁻¹(y − x) are Lipschitz, so they map Hᵏ-null sets to Hᵏ-null sets.
Choose R with spt f ⊆ B_R(0) and δ with B_δ(x) ⊆ V; for r < δ/R the blow-up integrands vanish off the open set η_r(V).
Hence each blow-up integral over η_r(S) equals the one over η_r(S ∩ V).
On η_r(M ∩ V) the weights θ(x+r·) and θ′(x+r·) agree a.e., and η_r(M∩V), η_r(M′∩V) are a.e. equal.
The blow-up integrals of (M,θ) and (M′,θ′) coincide for all small r and θ(x) = θ′(x), so the limits and hence the weighted tangent spaces agree.

subproblems.title: If M(X) < ∞, then ω ↦ X(χω) is a current on ℝ^P
subproblems.statement: Let P, q ∈ ℕ and let U ⊆ ℝ^P be an arbitrary set. Let χ : ℝ^P → ℝ be C^∞ (ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) χ) with tsupport χ ⊆ U and |χ(x)| ≤ 1 for every x. Let X ∈ D_q(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U q) have finite mass, M(X) = X.mass = X.massOn U ≠ ∞. Then there is Y ∈ D_q(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn univ q: a linear functional on D^q(ℝ^P) that is sequentially continuous at 0 in the sense of TestFormOnConverges) such that Y(ω) = X(η) for all ω ∈ D^q(ℝ^P) and η ∈ D^q(U) with η(x) = χ(x)·ω(x) for every x ∈ ℝ^P.

3. (Sequential continuity.) Let (ω_j) be a sequence in D^q(ℝ^P) with TestFormOnConverges ω 0. We show Y₀(ω_j) → 0.
   (a) By the reused sibling converges_small (Submission.fiw_ims_sc_converges_zero_small) with U := ℝ^P: for every δ > 0 there is j₀ such that |ω_j(x)| ≤ δ for all j ≥ j₀ and all x ∈ ℝ^P (eventually_atTop).

subproblems.title: Lemma A: a current on ℝ^P vanishing off a compact K ⊆ U has M(Z) ≤ M(Z|_U)

subproblems.title: Lemma B: if Z on ℝ^P vanishes off a compact K ⊆ U and Z|_U is integer multiplicity, then so is Z
subproblems.statement: Let P, q ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, K ⊆ U compact, and Z ∈ D_q(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn univ q) with Z(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ D^q(ℝ^P) whose tsupport is disjoint from K. Suppose Z|_U := Z.restrictDomain (subset_univ U) is an integer multiplicity current in U. That is, Z|_U = τ(M, θ, ξ) on D^q(U) for a rectifiable triple with IsRectifiableTriple U q M θ ξ and θ(x) ∈ ℕ for x ∈ M. Then Z is an integer multiplicity current in ℝ^P (IsIntegerMultiplicity Z, with a triple relative to univ).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P q : ℕ) (U K : Set (Eucl P)), IsOpen U → IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → ∀ Z : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Eucl P)) q, (∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Eucl P)) q, Disjoint (tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) q)) K → Z ω = 0) → IsIntegerMultiplicity (Z.restrictDomain (subset_univ U)) → IsIntegerMultiplicity Z
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 9 (Lemma B, (B1)–(B5)) of the parent proof.
- In (B2), the support-null fact H^q(M ∖ spt(Z|_U)) = 0 comes from the reused sibling rect_support_null (Submission.lpf_rectifiable_support_null). It has the same conclusion as the parent's sibling support_null, but no MF hypothesis.
- In (B3)–(B4), the blow-up/tangent congruence is the reused sibling tangent_congr (Submission.br_weightedTangent_congr). As the parent's Remark indicates, the special case used is V := ℝ^P, M' := M ∩ K, θ' := θ.

Notation.
- H := H^q = μHE[q], and H⌞A := H.restrict A.
- τ(M, θ, ξ)(φ) := tauAction q M θ ξ φ = ∫_M θ(x)·ξ(x)(φ(x)) dH(x).
- ι := testFormOnInclusion (subset_univ U) q; it does not change the underlying form.

1. (Data.) By hypothesis there are M, θ, ξ with:
   - IsRectifiableTriple U q M θ ξ;
   - θ(x) ∈ ℕ for every x ∈ M;
   - Z|_U(ω) = τ(M, θ, ξ)(ω) for every ω ∈ D^q(U).
2. ((B1): spt(Z|_U) ⊆ K.) Let ω ∈ D^q(U) with tsupport ω disjoint from K. Then Z|_U(ω) = Z(ιω) = 0 by the hypothesis on Z, since ιω has the same underlying form and hence the same tsupport. U is open, and K is closed (compact in the Hausdorff space ℝ^P). So the sibling support_subset with V := U gives spt(Z|_U) ⊆ K.
3. ((B2): H(M ∖ K) = 0.) The reused sibling rect_support_null, applied to T := Z|_U and the triple of step 1, gives H(M ∖ spt(Z|_U)) = 0. By step 2, M ∖ K ⊆ M ∖ spt(Z|_U), so H(M ∖ K) = 0 (measure_mono_null).
4. Put M' := M ∩ K.
   - M' ∖ M = ∅, and M ∖ M' = M ∖ K is H-null. So M' and M are H-a.e. equal (ae_eq_set), and H⌞M' = H⌞M (Measure.restrict_congr_set).
   - symmDiff M M' = (M ∖ M') ∪ (M' ∖ M) ⊆ M ∖ K, hence H(symmDiff M M' ∩ ℝ^P) = 0.
5. ((B3)–(B4): (M', θ, ξ) is a rectifiable triple in ℝ^P.) We verify the seven fields of IsRectifiableTriple univ q M' θ ξ.
   (a) subset: M' ⊆ ℝ^P = univ.
   (b) nullMeasurableSet: M is H-null-measurable and K is closed, hence measurable. So M' = M ∩ K is H-null-measurable (NullMeasurableSet.inter).
   (c) countablyRectifiable: M' ⊆ M, and M is countably q-rectifiable (CountablyRectifiable.mono).
   (d) pos: θ > 0 on M ⊇ M'.
   (e) integrableOn: let K'' ⊆ ℝ^P be compact. θ is H-integrable on M ∩ K, because K is a compact subset of U (field integrableOn of the U-triple). Since M' ∩ K'' ⊆ M ∩ K, θ is H-integrable on M' ∩ K'' (IntegrableOn.mono_set).
   (f) aestronglyMeasurable: ξ is a.e. strongly measurable for H⌞M = H⌞M' (step 4).
   (g) orients: since H⌞M' = H⌞M, it suffices to show the following for H⌞M-a.e. x: there is an orthonormal τ : Fin q → ℝ^P with HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt q M' θ x (span(range τ)) and ξ(x) = ±simpleNVector τ.
       - The U-triple gives, for H⌞M-a.e. x, an orthonormal τ with HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt q M θ x (span(range τ)) and ξ(x) = ±simpleNVector τ.
       - For such x, apply the reused sibling tangent_congr with (M, M', θ, θ', x, V) := (M, M', θ, θ, x, ℝ^P). Its hypotheses hold: ℝ^P is open and contains x; H(symmDiff M M' ∩ ℝ^P) = 0 by step 4; θ = θ everywhere; θ(x) = θ(x).
       - It gives HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt q M' θ x (span(range τ)), so the same τ works (filter_upwards).
6. (Integrality.) For x ∈ M' ⊆ M, θ(x) ∈ ℕ by step 1.
7. ((B5): representation.)
   - The sibling cutoff gives a C^∞ χ with tsupport χ ⊆ U and an open N ⊇ K with χ = 1 on N.
   - The sibling smul_testform (V := ℝ^P, W := U) gives a linear L : D^q(ℝ^P) → D^q(U) with (Lω)(x) = χ(x)·ω(x).
   Let ω ∈ D^q(ℝ^P).
   (a) ι(Lω) and ω agree on N, because χ = 1 there. So the sibling eq_near (V := ℝ^P, with the vanishing hypothesis on Z) gives Z(ω) = Z(ι(Lω)) = Z|_U(Lω).
   (b) By step 1 and H⌞M = H⌞M' (step 4): Z|_U(Lω) = ∫_M θ(x)·ξ(x)(χ(x)ω(x)) dH(x) = ∫_{M'} θ(x)·ξ(x)(χ(x)ω(x)) dH(x).
   (c) For x ∈ M' we have x ∈ K ⊆ N, so χ(x) = 1 and θ(x)·ξ(x)(χ(x)ω(x)) = θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(x)). M' is H-null-measurable (5(b)), so setIntegral_congr_fun₀ gives ∫_{M'} θ·ξ(χω) dH = ∫_{M'} θ·ξ(ω) dH = τ(M', θ, ξ)(ω).
   Hence Z(ω) = τ(M', θ, ξ)(ω) for every ω ∈ D^q(ℝ^P).
8. By steps 5, 6 and 7, (M', θ, ξ) witnesses IsIntegerMultiplicity Z. ∎

theorem Submission.fiw_tb_ext_isIntegerMultiplicity : ∀ (P q : ℕ) (U K : Set (Eucl P)), IsOpen U → IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → ∀ Z : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Eucl P)) q, (∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Eucl P)) q, Disjoint (tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) q)) K → Z ω = 0) → IsIntegerMultiplicity (Z.restrictDomain (subset_univ U)) → IsIntegerMultiplicity Z := by
  intro P q U K hU hK hKU Z hZ hIM
  obtain ⟨M, θ, ξ, htri, hθN, hrep⟩ := hIM
  have hZUv : ∀ ω : TestFormOn U q, Disjoint (tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) q)) K →
      (Z.restrictDomain (subset_univ U)) ω = 0 := fun ω hω => hZ _ hω
  have hsptU : (Z.restrictDomain (subset_univ U)).support ⊆ K :=
    Submission.fiw_tb_ext_support_subset P q U K _ hU hK.isClosed hZUv
  have hnull : (μHE[q] : Measure (Eucl P)) (M \ K) = 0 :=
    measure_mono_null (sdiff_subset_sdiff_right hsptU)
      (Submission.lpf_rectifiable_support_null P q U _ M θ ξ htri hrep)
  have hae : (M ∩ K : Set (Eucl P)) =ᵐ[(μHE[q] : Measure (Eucl P))] M := by
    rw [ae_eq_set]
    constructor
    · exact measure_mono_null (fun x hx => (hx.2 hx.1.1).elim) measure_empty
    · simpa [sdiff_inter_self_eq_sdiff] using hnull
  have hrestr : (μHE[q] : Measure (Eucl P)).restrict (M ∩ K) =
      (μHE[q] : Measure (Eucl P)).restrict M := Measure.restrict_congr_set hae
  have hsymm : (μHE[q] : Measure (Eucl P)) (symmDiff M (M ∩ K) ∩ univ) = 0 := by
    refine measure_mono_null (fun x hx => ?_) hnull
    rcases hx.1 with ⟨hxM, hxMK⟩ | ⟨hxMK, hxM⟩
    · exact ⟨hxM, fun hxK => hxMK ⟨hxM, hxK⟩⟩
    · exact absurd hxMK.1 hxM
  have htri' : IsRectifiableTriple (univ : Set (Eucl P)) q (M ∩ K) θ ξ :=
    { subset := subset_univ _
      nullMeasurableSet := htri.nullMeasurableSet.inter hK.isClosed.measurableSet.nullMeasurableSet
      countablyRectifiable := htri.countablyRectifiable.mono inter_subset_left
      pos := fun x hx => htri.pos x hx.1
      integrableOn := fun K'' _ _ =>
        (htri.integrableOn K hK hKU).mono_set inter_subset_left
      aestronglyMeasurable := by rw [hrestr]; exact htri.aestronglyMeasurable
      orients := by
        rw [hrestr]
        filter_upwards [htri.orients] with x hx
        obtain ⟨τ, hτ, htan, hξ⟩ := hx
        exact ⟨τ, hτ, Submission.br_weightedTangent_congr P q M (M ∩ K) θ θ x univ isOpen_univ
          (mem_univ x) hsymm (ae_of_all _ fun _ => rfl) rfl _ htan, hξ⟩ }
  refine ⟨M ∩ K, θ, ξ, htri', fun x hx => hθN x hx.1, fun ω => ?_⟩
  obtain ⟨χ, N, hχs, -, -, hχU, hN, hKN, hχN⟩ := Submission.fiw_tb_ext_cutoff P U K hU hK hKU
  obtain ⟨L, hL⟩ := Submission.fiw_tb_ext_smul_testForm P q (univ : Set (Eucl P)) U χ hχs hχU
  have h1 : Z ω = Z (testFormOnInclusion (subset_univ U) q (L ω)) :=
    (Submission.fiw_tb_ext_apply_eq_of_eqOn P q univ K N Z hN hKN hZ ω _ (fun x hx => by
      change (L ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) q) x = _
      rw [hL, hχN x hx, one_smul])).symm
  rw [h1, ← GeometricCurrentOn.restrictDomain_apply, hrep]
  unfold tauAction
  rw [← hrestr]
  apply setIntegral_congr_fun₀ htri'.nullMeasurableSet
  intro x hx
  change θ x * ξ x ((L ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) q) x) = _
  rw [hL, hχN x (hKN hx.2), one_smul]
proof_key_steps: (B1): Z|_U vanishes off K, so spt(Z|_U) ⊆ K by support_subset (U open).
(B2): rect_support_null gives H^q(M ∖ spt(Z|_U)) = 0. Hence H^q(M ∖ K) = 0 and H^q⌞(M ∩ K) = H^q⌞M.
(B3)–(B4): (M ∩ K, θ, ξ) is a rectifiable triple in ℝ^P; the orientation transfers by tangent_congr with V = ℝ^P.
(B5): Z(ω) = Z|_U(χω) (eq_near) = ∫_M θξ(χω) = ∫_{M∩K} θξ(ω), since χ = 1 on K.
Hence Z = τ(M ∩ K, θ, ξ) with integer θ, so IsIntegerMultiplicity Z.
